([[Federal Way, Washington]]) | college = [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2019) }} '''Jaden McDaniels''' (born September 29, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. He attended [[Federal Way High School]] in [[Federal Way, Washington]], where he was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and Washington [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] as a senior. McDaniels was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2019 class. ==High school career== McDaniels played basketball for [[Federal Way High School]] in [[Federal Way, Washington]]. As a freshman, he was teammates with his older brother [[Jalen McDaniels|Jalen]] and helped Federal Way win its second straight Class 4A state championship.{{cite web |last1=Cotterill |first1=TJ |title=Federal Way has one of the top basketball recruits in the country – a 6-foot-9 guard |url=https://www-1.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article189918159.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |accessdate=July 21, 2019 |date=December 14, 2017}} McDaniels averaged 2.4 points and 1.8 rebounds per game on the [[varsity team]] and was forced to shoot with his left hand due to a right elbow injury.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=‘The future of basketball’ plays at Federal Way High School. His name is Jaden McDaniels. |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/hes-the-future-of-basketball-federal-ways-jaden-mcdaniels-has-become-one-of-the-best-in-nation/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=July 21, 2019 |date=February 20, 2019}} In his first two years, he helped his team win 63 consecutive games, the longest win streak in state history since 1977. As a junior, McDaniels guided Federal Way to a runner-up finish at the 4A state tournament.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=Gonzaga Prep rallies past Federal Way for 4A state boys championship |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/gonzaga-prep-rallies-past-federal-way-for-4a-state-boys-championship/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=July 21, 2019 |date=March 3, 2018}} In the season, he averaged 21.3 points, 10 rebounds, 4.6 assists, and 3.3 blocks per game and earned ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Washington first team honors.{{cite web |title=2017-18 ALL-USA Washington Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-washington-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=July 21, 2019 class.{{cite web |title=Washington forward Jaden McDaniels is EYBL's biggest spring stock-booster 2019}} ===Recruiting=== By the end of his high school career, McDaniels was considered a consensus five-star recruit and the best [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] in the 2019 class.{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels, Federal Way, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jaden-McDaniels-46046881/high-school-200372/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=July 22, 2019}} [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] ranked him among the top 10 players in his class.{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels, 2019 Power forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/jaden-mcdaniels-208389 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |accessdate=July 22, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/234172/jaden-mcdaniels |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=July 22, 2019}} On May 22, 2019, McDaniels committed to play college basketball for [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. He had also received strong interest from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] during the recruiting process.{{cite web |title=UW scores second top-7 recruit in PF McDaniels |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26798303/uw-scores-second-top-7-recruit-pf-mcdaniels |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=July 22, 2019 |date=May 22, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Jaden McDaniels | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Federal Way, Washington|Federal Way, WA]] | highschool = [[Federal Way High School|Federal Way]] (WA) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 185 | 40 = | commitdate = May 21, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Washington 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Washington Huskies Recruiting Class | rivals school = washington | scout s = | espn schoolid = 264 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 7 | 247 overall = 13 | espn overall = 7 | accessdate = April 5, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Jaden McDaniels.jpg|thumb|McDaniels (right) at the [[2019 Diamond Head Classic]]]] In his collegiate debut, a 67–64 upset of [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], McDaniels had 18 points and seven rebounds.{{cite news |title=Washington rallies, stuns No. 16 Baylor 67-64 in Alaska |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169602 |accessdate=November 11, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2019}} He had a season-high 22 points against [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]]. As a freshman, McDaniels averaged 13 points and 5.8 rebounds per game while starting 21 games but he began coming off the bench midway through conference play. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Washington freshman Jaden McDaniels declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29039539/washington-freshman-jaden-mcdaniels-declares-nba-draft |accessdate=April 15, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 15, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] | 31 || 21 || 31.1 || .405 || .339 || .763 || 5.8 || 2.1 || .8 || 1.4 || 13.0 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== McDaniels' brother, [[Jalen McDaniels]], played basketball for Federal Way High School, where he was a four-star recruit,{{cite web |last1=Ruiz |first1=Drew |title=NBA-Bound Jalen and Jaden McDaniels are Pushing Each Other into the Next Gear |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/mcdaniels-feat/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=July 21, 2019 |date=October 22, 2018}} before joining [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] at the college level. He was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=2019 Draft Prospect - Jalen McDaniels |url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2019/prospects/jalen-mcdaniels#/ |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |accessdate=July 21, 2019}} McDaniels is a cousin of former NBA player [[Juwan Howard]].
